notes.title: Patch Notes - v1.4.10
notes.content:
So my 6 yo is now old enough to save the planet and we've been playing together for a while now. He likes the game a lot: he's been running around the house carrying heavy things over his head, shouting "Opi STRONG". :)

His favourite is Curi, though. Curi's ability to evade Mowers is really appealing to him. Sometimes he activated hover at the wrong moment, so that Curi hovered just barely above the ground, which lead to some unscheduled Mower-induced disassemblies. He's very prudent and mourns each lost robot with a groan.

Seeing this, I implemented a change that makes sure that Curi always keeps a safe distance from the ground. With this change, you can also solve this obstacle without pressing a single button.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/e092d1ce58770107e9d2a3af4dc6ff65e80b1073.gif[/img]

Very convenient, and also maybe a bit more logical, no?

My son likes to play Spiri, too! Teleportation is always fun. With Spiri, he's been bumping into doors while teleporting which made the experience a bit clumsy, so Spiri also got a new assist feature that helps with this.

I hope these changes will make your kids' life easier, too :)

notes.title: Patch Notes, 1.4.9
notes.content:
Hello there! 

I went for an other run, this time securing a victory via the plant-based strategy. I also got the Mr. Proper achievement for bringing back 100% of life. Only a single achievement to go until platinum, the dreaded Agoraphobe Run aka. Indoors Challange, in which you can only go outdoors if there are no indoors missions on the map, which makes it really hard to replenish TRUST. It took many weeks until I nailed it on stream, and there weren't even Drones and Turrets back then! 

[previewyoutube=cNW2tRgBcAo;full][/previewyoutube]

Although there were no shields either, so I'm full of hope for this run. Anyway I'll try it with this brand new build, featuring:

- ledge assist: sometimes I fell off of floating bridges with Curi, so I implemented a little assist feature that helps you land on them.
- filtering out shared levels you've already played
- our heroes now have little name-tags in dialogues.

Have fun!
Andras

notes.title: Tweaks, tweaks everywhere!
notes.content:
So I returned to the game after not playing for a while and had an amazing run! I lost the run on [url=http://www.terraforming.earth/map#10-43722654-20-b-l-31]this crazy boss map[/url] but it was still awesome. I wish the game saved little GIFs when robots blow up, I had some pretty funny cases of the old total-party-kill-explosions 😈. I was amazed again by the sheer amount of details that our heroic visual artists put into the game, can't thank them enough for working with me on this game. <3 

Anyway I tweaked some parameters to make the experience more enjoyable, I hope these little things will make your runs more fun in the future!

- faster terraforming progress
- robots start on max TRUST
- longer spawn protection
- Spiri is protected from bullets while phasing
- perks from EPA depot and S.C.F comms tower hacks are more effective

To the stars and beyond!

notes.title: Turret Trouble - OUT NOW!
notes.content:
After Mowers and Drones, the cast of anti-heroes is now complete: Turrets are finally here!

[previewyoutube=u_475Hb1RcM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Bullet Hell... Puzzles?[/h2]

The free [b]Turret Trouble[/b] Update pits you against plasma-spewing enemies: you can't fight them directly, so you have to rely on your wit and planning abilities to make sure your quirky robots reach the objectives safely. 

Turret Trouble adds 20 new obstacle configurations to the existing 90 puzzle types, raising the number of unique Terraforming Earth levels to about 10^81, more than the number of atoms in the Universe.

We played and playtested this update for a long time now and we hope you'll like the extra intensity as much as we do. Have fun!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1029220/Terraforming_Earth/

notes.title: Get Ready for Some Turret Trouble
notes.content:
We are proud to introduce the latest entry on the [b]List of Things That Make Terraforming Difficult[/b]:

[h1]Turrets![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/8004fb4dab5a7cb68cc2ef29fe5043b57c23bd31.gif[/img]

Be very afraid.

[h2]Bullet Hell Puzzles[/h2]

Our latest expansion, [b]Turret Trouble[/b] introduces a ton of new puzzles and hazards. In the spirit of the previous set of foes, Mobile Turrets and their stationary counterparts make the levels more challenging and require careful planning to make sure that our heroes safely get to objectives and reach the exit in one piece. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/1e28faebba9735c8bd5f433b97bdc67bb2b59814.png[/img]

Annoying as these enemy robots might be, you also really need them to solve certain obstacles. You need Mowers to get higher and you need the Drones to fly over things. Likewise, you'll need the Turrets to... well, you'll figure it out :)

[h2]Quality of Life[/h2]

Turrets are the major attraction of this update, but we've also improved the experience in many different ways and polished the game in places we didn't even know could use some extra polish. This includes tweaking with controls to make Opi and Spiri more fun to drive around, better gamepad experience and a whole new intro sequence that teaches new players how to use the Factory and the Mission Control screens. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/b46e3e5c9e6d3cd1e3e4d4525701e56c565c0d44.png[/img]

The first three missions are now selected by hand to make sure players have time to get used to the controls before diving into the deep end of the procedurally generated pool.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/c64c3f323c28aef1315ff4324556504d09d5de03.png[/img]

Players who are flying solo will hugely appreciate that our heroes are now protected with cloaking devices when standing still. You don't need to park your robots carefully before switching to another one, freeing up a ton of mental resources so that you can concentrate on the puzzles. 

[h2]Coming Early Next Week[/h2]

Turrets will make their debut next week. If you are eager to meet them before the official release, hop onto our [url=https://discord.gg/cHT4f24]Discord server[/url] to learn the secret cheat code that unlocks them right now!

Cheers,
Andras and the Lost Robots team

notes.title: DRONE DANGER - Free DLC Out Now
notes.content:
[h2]Take a ride on Hermes Express[/h2]

The Hermes Express cargo drones are available to all players with today's update v1.1.0! 

[previewyoutube=fljhYWYjdks;full][/previewyoutube]

Free DLC Drone Danger introduces cargo drones – flying robots that are dangerous to hang around but can be used to solve new types of puzzles. Drone Danger is bringing you the Dark Souls of puzzle platforming with even more tricky situations and hilarious ways to die. Yes, this is a thinking-heavy puzzle game where things are chasing you and so won’t let you think. It doesn’t make sense. You should try it. :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/e57bfdd8869229ec1b96e6e35378fd2a85ae340b.png[/img]

[h2]Drones are so hard, we made them optional[/h2]

We've been playtesting Drones for 3 months now and we love the complexity they introduce to the vanilla game. 

Since the levels are designed with an obstacle-based approach (instead of using pre-defined rooms), the 10 new puzzle types can now combine randomly with the 70 vanilla puzzles resulting in an exponential explosion of complexity and a vast number of crazy new situations.

Actually the game gets so hard with these flying hazards that we introduced the option to turn them off. You can re-enable Drones at any time in the Settings!

Drone Danger also introduces two new achievements, one for completing the game with Drones enabled and, pssst, a secret one :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/64544edf3747f02408b17f988714bfe52a131bc3.png[/img]

This is a great opportunity to jump back in the game, and in case you haven't already, please consider picking up a copy now :)

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1029220/Terraforming_Earth/

notes.title: Cargo Drones Coming on March 6
notes.content:
The first major update introducing Hermes Cargo Drones is coming out on March 6.

[h2]HERMES GLOBAL CARGO DRONES[/h2]
By the end of the 21st century, Alfabeta Inc. has achieved its mission statement of organizing the world's matter and making it universally accessible and useful. Their algorithms have long figured out what everybody needs at any given time and so the vast majority of humans have signed up for Universal Matter Subscriptions, whereby Hermes Global Cargo Drones automatically fulfill every material need and desire 24/7. 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/e283b11688704bbc7208bda4fbf5f97be117da28.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/64c903f4956414b56aec26c0433db84380b50fdd.png[/img][/url]

After the global extinction event of 2087, nobody's around to cancel their subscriptions so the drones are roaming the planet, fulfilling orders on autopilot.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/94ecf324bacdb1f2da2079001945df8c156aef0d.png[/img]

Like EPA's trusty landscaping robots, cargo drones are both your friends and foes at the same time. They are very dangerous to hang around and introduce many tricky situations that you can only overcome by positioning your robots carefully. However, you can also exploit the drones by jumping on top of them to fly around and reach higher places. Drones thus enable and introduce many new types of puzzles, which combine with the basic puzzles of vanilla Terraforming Earth in unexpected ways, massively expanding the experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/64544edf3747f02408b17f988714bfe52a131bc3.png[/img]

We have been playtesting Drones for three months now and we are quite happy with the variety and the extra complexity they introduce to the basic game. They also really highlight the roguelike-like aspect of the game, where mistakes have grave consequences and you have to think quickly to stay alive. 

[h2]INTERPOLATION: WHERE YOUR CANDID GAME DESIGNER IS TRYING TO FIGURE OUT WHO THIS GAME REALLY IS FOR[/h2]
This leads us to the realization that Terraforming Earth is not really a game for traditional puzzle lovers who like to take their time figuring out the puzzles at their own pace. Time pressure and dangerous things chasing you have gone out of vogue in the puzzle game genre for very good reasons. Solving the same puzzle level twice is excruciating, so killing the player and forcing them to restart is a very bad game design pattern indeed. 

However, Terraforming Earth's level designer AI invents a whole new genre of puzzle games: the [b]Roguelike Puzzle-Platformer[/b]. Since each level is freshly baked in your computer just for you, I can get away with making your life challenging and introducing permanent failure. By failing to solve an unfamiliar situation, you have learned an important lesson about the game (and the real world), which makes your following runs more manageable and that much richer. So and since each run is new and unique, there's no excruciating repetition. Just nearly endless learning and training your pattern-matching circuits for this game in particular and your problem-solving skills for life in general.

Terraforming Earth might not appeal to most traditional roguelike fans either, is what I'm grappling with lately. Since the combination of puzzles requires a fair amount of deliberate thinking, you can't rely on instinctive skill-of-hand alone to complete levels. Instead of simply getting good at combat you have to expend precious cognitive resources every time, in every situation. It's more like [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_boxing]chess boxing[/url] where you have to master two wildly different disciplines to be successful. Like chess boxing, Terraforming Earth will likely have a very niche audience. After all, who on Earth enjoys pondering optimal chess moves while getting pounded in the ring? Who on Earth enjoys finding their way through intricate mazes while being chased down by deadly drones and [url=https://youtu.be/VOIodZEJwow?t=5841]nanobot swarms[/url]?

I do. I really do. And you might, too. We have no idea. This is a completely new gaming genre and it doesn't have a target audience yet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/94adeb200fdef50c05c0da5aa3246e00adabf20e.png[/img]

[h2]CHALLENGES OPTIONAL[/h2]
Our candid game designer's insecurities aside, Terraforming Earth appeals to a wide range of players. Perma-death, time pressure, and drones are all optional. You can complete the game without solving brutal Patient Zero maps (such as the one linked above under [i]nanobot swarms[/i]). 

Puzzle lovers can take their time and are rewarded with increasingly large and complex mazes, speedrunners can compete on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1029220/discussions/0/1745644671662806776/]weekly challenges[/url], couples and families can take delight in the marvel of teamwork, explorers can find and promote cool maps for the community, environmentalists will love the theme and the stunning visuals of life returning to the planet, etc, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34575508/521992b612ee1bc57362549be7535bc3a329bd1d.png[/img]

OK, now that we have convinced everyone that Terraforming Earth is super fun, let's eagerly await the Drones' debut on March 6, 2020 :)

Meanwhile, you can buy Terraforming Earth right now and enjoy the vanilla edition with tons of puzzles, unique post-apocalyptic environments and a complete, crazy story about quirky robots and AI-risk!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1029220/Terraforming_Earth/

Thanks for reading!
Andras (Lost Robots)
